sources.label: ChromeStatus feature 5111997147512832 — CSS URL request modifiers

outputs.rationale: cross-origin() is a declarative CSS functional notation inside url(); it configures the fetch and returns no programmable value.

errors.rationale: The page documents no failure or error behavior for cross-origin(); its table row lists accepted values and CORS effect only.

lifecycle.rationale: Declarative CSS parsed at style resolution; cross-origin() has no runtime instantiation, event, or teardown lifecycle.

outputs.rationale: integrity() is a declarative CSS functional notation inside url(); it configures the fetch and returns no programmable value.

lifecycle.rationale: Declarative CSS parsed at style resolution; integrity() has no runtime instantiation, event, or teardown lifecycle.

outputs.rationale: referrer-policy() is a declarative CSS functional notation inside url(); it configures the fetch and returns no programmable value.

errors.rationale: The page documents no failure or error behavior for referrer-policy(); its table row lists accepted values and referrer effect only.

lifecycle.rationale: Declarative CSS parsed at style resolution; referrer-policy() has no runtime instantiation, event, or teardown lifecycle.

notes: B4 unit: the page carried zero id attributes, so five existing headings gained ids (why-it-exists, syntax, example, browser-support, see-also) and nothing else in the page changed; the three canonical ids are syntax (on 'shape of the API'), browser-support, and see-also, with example and why-it-exists added so the examples and context dimensions map to slices that actually contain that content (pattern matched to landed v150/css-text-fit-property). No code block was added because the page already ships one. Inventory is the page's own shape table: the three modifier functions, each kind css-function. Not-applicable dimensions and their gaps: outputs and lifecycle for all three functions (declarative CSS notation, no return value, no runtime lifecycle); errors for cross-origin() and referrer-policy() only — the page documents no failure behavior for those two (integrity() IS documented, its row states the fetch fails on hash mismatch). Sources verified 2026-10-07: ChromeStatus record confirms feature name, milestone 150 desktop/android/webview with flag=false and origintrial=false, Firefox view 5 = No signal, Safari view 1 = Shipped/Shipping; the modifier grammar (cross-origin( anonymous | use-credentials ), integrity( <string> ), referrer-policy( <valid policy> )) matches CSS Values 5 §4.1.1. Observation, not a divergence: the ChromeStatus record's status field still reads 'Proposed' with is_released=false because the record was last updated 2026-06-09, before Chrome 150 stable (current stable is 155 per versionhistory.googleapis.com); every operative shipping token on the page (milestone 150, all platforms, enabled by default with no flag or origin trial) is confirmed by the record.
